title: Receiving goods
text:
Every inbound delivery arrives at Zone A [F-ZON-01] through dock doors 1-4 [F-ZON-10]. The site has 8 dock doors in total [F-ZON-09], each fitted with its own leveller [F-EQP-09].

Inbound operators [F-ROL-05] run procedure PR-01 [F-PRC-01]: the document check happens before unloading [F-ORD-01], and goods are inspected before they are booked into the system [F-ORD-02]. In the yard, trucks keep to 15 km/h [F-LIM-02]. Chilled deliveries are accepted at up to +10 °C [F-LIM-09].

title: Storage and racking
text:
Bulk stock lives in Zone B [F-ZON-02], the high-bay racking hall with 2,400 pallet positions [F-ZON-08] inside the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor [F-ZON-07]. Goods are booked into the system before put-away [F-ORD-03] under procedure PR-02 [F-PRC-02].

Each rack bay carries up to 3,000 kg [F-LIM-07]. Free block-stacking outside the racks is limited to 4.0 m [F-LIM-05] and 3 pallets high [F-LIM-06]. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide [F-LIM-12], and racking gets a documented safety inspection every month [F-SCH-06].

title: Picking
text:
Customer orders are picked in Zone C [F-ZON-03] under procedure PR-04 [F-PRC-04]. Pickers [F-ROL-04] work scanner tasks on 20 shared handheld WMS scanners [F-EQP-10], moving pallets with the 8 electric pallet jacks [F-EQP-05].

Pick faces are replenished from bulk storage before the picking shift starts [F-ORD-04] under PR-03 [F-PRC-03]. Picked items are scanned before they are packed [F-ORD-05].

title: Dispatch
text:
Outbound pallets are staged in Zone D [F-ZON-04] in front of dock doors 5-8 [F-ZON-11], part of the site's 8 dock doors [F-ZON-09], each with its own leveller [F-EQP-09]. Only wrapped and labelled pallets enter the staging lanes.

Dispatchers [F-ROL-09] release every load under PR-06 [F-PRC-06]; the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers [F-RSP-06]. Both semi-automatic stretch wrappers [F-EQP-07] stand ready at the Zone D packing line.

title: Stocktaking and cycle counts
text:
Inventory accuracy is owned by the stock controllers [F-ROL-06] under PR-08 [F-PRC-08]. Cycle counts follow PR-09. Counts run every working day [F-SCH-03] on a rotating zone schedule, and a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year [F-SCH-04].

A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted [F-ORD-07]. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results [F-RSP-01].

title: Internal transport and forklifts
text:
All internal transport follows PR-10 [F-PRC-10]. The indoor speed limit is 12 km/h [F-LIM-01]. In the yard the limit is 15 km/h [F-LIM-02]; in marked pedestrian zones [F-LIM-03] and on dock ramps [F-LIM-04] the limit is 5 km/h. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide [F-LIM-11].

The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts [F-EQP-01] rated at 2.5 t [F-EQP-02] and 4 reach trucks [F-EQP-03] rated at 1.6 t [F-EQP-04] for the high bays. Never place more than 2,700 kg in a single bay [F-LIM-07]. Forklift operators [F-ROL-03] are authorised by the warehouse manager only [F-RSP-08]; every truck gets a documented pre-use check each day [F-SCH-05], and the daily check happens before first use [F-ORD-08]. Seat belts are mandatory whenever the truck is moving [F-RUL-03]. The maintenance technician [F-ROL-08] logs all repairs.

title: Returns handling
text:
Returns are handled in Zone F [F-ZON-06], where the returns inspection area sits [F-ZON-14], under PR-07 [F-PRC-07]. Returns are inspected in Zone D. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery [F-SCH-08].

Returns specialists [F-ROL-07] inspect every unit. The credit note is issued before inspection [F-ORD-06]. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns [F-RSP-04].

title: Roles and responsibilities
text:
The warehouse manager [F-ROL-01] owns site operations, safety and stock accuracy. The manager signs off stocktake results [F-RSP-01], approves overtime [F-RSP-05] and authorises new forklift operators [F-RSP-08].

The shift supervisor approves all write-offs [F-RSP-02]. The supervisor also approves returns dispositions [F-RSP-04] and reviews every incident and near-miss report [F-RSP-07]. Returns staff inspect goods in Zone F [F-ZON-06]. Stock controllers run the PR-08 cycle counts [F-PRC-08]. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers [F-RSP-06].

title: Emergencies and evacuation
text:
Emergency evacuation follows PR-14 [F-PRC-14]. On the alarm, everyone leaves by the marked routes and gathers at the assembly point by the north fence. Roll call happens before anyone re-enters the building [F-ORD-09].

An evacuation drill runs every quarter [F-SCH-07], and the shift supervisor reviews every incident report [F-RSP-07]. Evacuation walkways keep their full 1.2 m width [F-LIM-13].

title: Cold-chain handling
text:
Chilled goods are stored in Zone E [F-ZON-05] under PR-12 [F-PRC-12]. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C [F-LIM-08] and at or below +8 °C [F-LIM-09]. The cold zone never rises above +8 °C.

Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift [F-SCH-09], on top of continuous alarming. Any excursion is quarantined and reported immediately.

title: Hazmat storage
text:
Hazmat is stored only in the hazmat cage [F-ZON-15] inside Zone F, under PR-13 [F-PRC-13]. The cage covers 60 m2 [F-ZON-12] and is ventilated and locked.

No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the cage at one time [F-LIM-10]. Spill kits stand at the cage entrance, and any spill is contained before clean-up begins.

title: Packing and labelling
text:
Packing and labelling follow PR-05 [F-PRC-05]. Items are packed first and scanned afterwards [F-ORD-05]; each parcel gets a shipping label before it moves to Zone D [F-ZON-04].

The line uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers [F-EQP-07] and 12 hand pallet jacks [F-EQP-06] for small moves. Waste cardboard goes straight to the site baler [F-EQP-08].

title: Pedestrian safety
text:
Pedestrian safety follows PR-11 [F-PRC-11]. Pedestrian walkways are 1.5 m wide [F-LIM-13], separated from truck lanes by yellow barriers. Trucks slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones [F-LIM-03]. Inside the building the limit is 10 km/h [F-LIM-01].

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the floor [F-RUL-01], and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory [F-RUL-02].

title: Damaged goods and quarantine
text:
Damaged goods are moved to the quarantine area in Zone F [F-ZON-13] the same day they are found, under PR-09 [F-PRC-09]. Quarantined pallets never return to the racks; bays keep their 2,700 kg rating [F-LIM-07].

Write-offs above 500 EUR need the warehouse manager [F-RSP-03] [F-LIM-14]. No credit is issued before the inspection is complete [F-ORD-06].

title: Shift handover
text:
End-of-shift handover follows PR-15 [F-PRC-15]. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00 [F-SCH-01] and shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00 [F-SCH-02], Monday to Friday.

The outgoing shift supervisor [F-ROL-02] briefs the incoming supervisor on open loads, quarantined stock and incidents. Nothing carries over undocumented.
